name: Denton
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Denton, TX 2026
seo_description: Denton Holiday Lighting Festival, Wassail Fest in Downtown Denton on Dec 5, Santa at the Station on the DCTA A-train and Santa at Golden Triangle Mall.
lede: The story of Christmas in Denton begins on the courthouse lawn, where neighbors raised money in 1988 to light the trees around the Courthouse-on-the-Square and started the Denton Holiday Lighting Festival. Since 1999 downtown has added Wassail Fest, when shops around the Square pour warm spiced cider for the whole town.
sections: The courthouse lawn lights, lit since 1988

In 1988 a group of Denton neighbors formed the Denton Holiday Festival Association, a nonprofit, to raise money to light the trees on the lawn of the Courthouse-on-the-Square. The festival has been held every year since, and it grew to include stages of music and dance, children's crafts, visits with Santa, horse-drawn carriage rides and a toy drive for families in need. The Denton Record-Chronicle reports that it usually draws 17,000 to 20,000 people. In 2023 the organizers moved the start from 6 pm to 3 pm to spread out the crowds, and the night still ends the way it began: the lights come on and Santa Claus arrives.

Wassail Fest started in 1999 with the Denton Main Street Association, and the City of Denton Main Street Program runs it today. The city describes it as a festive Main Street tradition that celebrates the English custom of wassailing, sharing warm spiced cider made with citrus and spices like cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger and cloves. Downtown businesses compete with their own recipes, and the Main Street program says each one usually serves between 1,200 and 3,000 small samples. The samples are non-alcoholic and family friendly, and visitors vote for a favorite. For years it ran the night before the Holiday Lighting Festival; in 2026 it moves to the Saturday afternoon of the festival.
Riding the A-train to see Santa

Denton is the northern end of the DCTA A-train. The Denton County Transportation Authority began running the commuter line on June 20, 2011, from Denton southwest through Lewisville to Trinity Mills Station in Carrollton, where riders change to DART's Green Line toward Dallas. Its stations include the Downtown Denton Transit Center, MedPark, Highland Village/Lewisville Lake, Old Town and Hebron. At Christmas DCTA turns the line into a Santa train: Santa at the Station takes families from the downtown transit center to Trinity Mills and back with Santa and the Holly Jolly Elf on board. For a longer train day, the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco and the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano are a short drive away.

faq: When did the Denton Holiday Lighting Festival start?

In 1988 a group of Denton neighbors formed the Denton Holiday Festival Association, a nonprofit, to raise money to light the trees on the lawn of the Courthouse-on-the-Square. The festival has been held every year since and grew to include music, crafts, Santa, carriage rides and a toy drive.
How many people come to the Denton Holiday Lighting Festival?

The Denton Record-Chronicle reports that it usually draws 17,000 to 20,000 people. In 2023 the organizers moved the start from 6 pm to 3 pm to spread out the crowds, and the night still ends with the lights coming on and Santa Claus arriving.
What is Wassail Fest in Denton?

Wassail Fest started in 1999 with the Denton Main Street Association, and the City of Denton Main Street Program runs it today. Downtown businesses serve warm, non alcoholic spiced cider samples, and visitors vote for a favorite. In 2026 it is Saturday, December 5, from 3 to 5 pm.
Can kids ride a Santa train in Denton?

Yes. DCTA runs Santa at the Station, a Santa ride on the A-train from the Downtown Denton Transit Center to Trinity Mills and back, with Santa and the Holly Jolly Elf on board. The 2026 ride is Saturday, December 5. The A-train began running on June 20, 2011.
Who organizes Christmas events in Denton?

The Denton Holiday Festival Association founded the Holiday Lighting Festival, and the City of Denton Main Street Program runs Wassail Fest. DCTA, the Denton County Transportation Authority, runs Santa at the Station. Downtown Denton also posts partner events for the season.
